one_month_reasoning: Main scheduled event: Q3 2026 results. Uber hasn't confirmed the date yet, but last year's Q3 call was Nov 4, 2025 at 5am PT (src 10), so Q3 2026 most likely lands Nov 3-4, 2026, before the open and inside the window (I put ~75% on it). Guidance is $58.25-60.25B gross bookings and $0.84-0.88 non-GAAP EPS (src 1,4). Uber beat the top of its bookings guide in Q2 and has posted four straight quarters of 20%+ growth (src 3), so a beat on the quarter is likely. The stock reaction will turn on the Q4 guide, buyback restart ('months, not quarters', src 3) and any P&L sizing of the $10B AV program. That is two-sided, since the Q2 guide drew a -5% reaction. The Delivery Hero acceptance period ends Nov 5 (src 8), the day after the window, and only the 50%+1 threshold is in question because Uber already holds ~53% economic interest. Short-horizon drift: negative 12-month momentum against open-market insider buying near the lows (CEO $10M at $70.96, src 9). I treat these as roughly offsetting. So the forecast is close to symmetric around spot, median ~$69.9, log-sd 0.11 (annual vol 35%/3.5 = 10%, widened slightly for the earnings print).

fair_value.method: Blend of 50% P/E (18x NTM non-GAAP EPS at horizon of ~$4.70 = $84.6) and 50% SBC-adjusted FCF yield (7% on ~$5.80/share NTM FCF less SBC = $83). Both multiples sit below the peer median because of AV disintermediation risk.

inputs_detail.derivation: 0.72+0.81+0.86 plus Q4 ~$0.93 (Q3 midpoint +8% seq., in line with the Q2->Q3 step). +35% vs FY25, matching 28-44% YoY quarterly growth. Non-GAAP EPS here is burdened by SBC: Adj. EBITDA minus non-GAAP op. income (~$0.6-0.7B/qtr) equals D&A plus SBC (src 1,5).

Bookings growing 18-22% cc (guide) with incremental margin expansion (non-GAAP op. margin 3.7% of GB, +40bp YoY), ~3-4% annual net share-count decline (diluted shares -4% YoY), and CA insurance savings from 2027 (src 4). Consensus 3Y EPS CAGR is ~31% (src 13) and FY27 consensus EPS $4.56 (src 12, may mix GAAP). I haircut both for AV investment P&L drag the CFO said will come (src 3). FY27 ~$4.15, FY28 ~$4.98.
0.25 x FY27 $4.15 + 0.75 x FY28 $4.98 = $4.77, rounded down to $4.70 for pre-close Delivery Hero acquisition debt carry (EUR14.2B bridge, src 7).

Peer median fwd P/E is 26.0x (range 8.0x-209x, 11 peers). Uber trades at 16.8x fwd today (src 13). 18x is inside the range and near CART/GRAB (17.7x/18.2x), above mature travel (BKNG 14.3x, EXPE 11.7x), well below DASH 28x. The discount to the median reflects robotaxi disintermediation risk that won't resolve before 2028 (src 3, 11).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF ~$13.8B less SBC ~$2.3B = $11.5B / ~1.98B diluted shares = ~$5.80; at 7% yield

inputs_detail.derivation: TTM $10.1B grown ~18-20%/yr (in line with EPS/EBITDA growth of 33% slowing). FY27 ~$12.3B, FY28 ~$14.3B, blended NTM ~$13.8B. AV equity and fleet support sits mostly in investing cash flow (src 3).
2.050B diluted Q2'26 (src 1), 2.043B outstanding Jul 31 (src 2). ~50% of FCF to buybacks (src 3) is ~$5-6B/yr, retiring ~75M shares at ~$75, less SBC issuance. ~$16B authorization remains (src 4).

Uber trades at ~13.8x P/FCF (7.3% yield, src 13). Peers BKNG/EXPE trade at ~10-12x EV/EBITDA and DASH/ABNB at ~30-57x (src 14). 7% is a modest re-rate only, reflecting growth above mature travel names but AV terminal-value risk.

bear.story: Tesla Cybercab (Austin, Sep-2026) and Waymo scale faster than expected and the market prices permanent loss of the US Mobility profit pool. Bookings growth slows to low-mid teens, the AV P&L drag is sized larger than feared, and Delivery Hero integration risk plus ~2x leverage weigh. ~11.5x on ~$4.3 NTM EPS.

base.story: High-teens bookings growth, ~25% EPS growth, buybacks resume, and AV partner launches (15 cities by YE26, LA/SF 2027) show Uber as a distribution layer, though the market keeps a discount. ~17x on $4.70.

bull.story: AV cities on Uber show category growth (as in SF/LA/Phoenix, src 3), Delivery Hero closes on schedule with credible $1.2B synergies, CA insurance savings flow, and the multiple re-rates toward ~21x on ~$5.0. That roughly matches the Street mean target of ~$101.

comps_summary.peer_range: Fwd P/E 7.97x (LYFT) to 208.97x (Eternal), interquartile ~14x-32x. EV/EBITDA 10.5x (EXPE) to 165x (Eternal). Note: the EV/EBITDA figures are the source's headline (trailing) ratios, because forward EV/EBITDA was not available. Meituan EV/EBITDA n/a (loss-making). Delivery Hero excluded, since it is pinned to Uber's EUR41.50 offer.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 18x NTM P/E: below the 26x median, inside the range, between CART/GRAB (~18x) and BKNG (14.3x). Uber's current EV/EBITDA of 19.3x (src 13) is below the ~28x median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: I take a discount, not a premium. Uber's growth (bookings 20%+, EPS ~30%) and margin trajectory would support a median multiple. But robotaxi disintermediation is a structural, unresolved risk through the horizon: BofA sees rivals with an 18-24 month lead and AV partnerships scaling only in 2028 (src 11). Uber has also committed ~$10B to AV whose P&L impact is not yet sized (src 3) and takes on ~EUR14B of bridge debt for Delivery Hero (src 7). The closest direct-risk peer (LYFT, 8x) trades far below the median, so I stay below the median rather than claim outperformance.

thesis_break_reason: $52 is ~11x my NTM EPS, a mature-travel/LYFT-type multiple. The stock would only trade there if the market concluded that (a) bookings growth is breaking toward ~10% (e.g. US Mobility share loss in Waymo/Tesla cities, reversing the Q2 acceleration in SF/LA/Phoenix), (b) the AV program turns into large recurring losses or balance-sheet fleet ownership, or (c) the Delivery Hero deal derails or leverage goes well above the 2x target. Ordinary 35%-vol moves from $70 rarely reach that level absent such news. The 52-week low of $65.41 is only volatility.

key_uncertainties: Pace of Waymo/Tesla/Zoox owned-app robotaxi scaling in Uber's top US cities, and whether AV supply joins Uber's network or bypasses it
P&L and FCF impact of the $10B multi-year AV investment program (not yet sized by management)
Delivery Hero: regulatory clearances, integration (migrations not until 2029), synergy delivery, leverage near 2x
Whether buybacks return to ~50% of FCF quickly ('months, not quarters')
FX turned to a ~1pt headwind in Q3; consumer cyclicality; ongoing take-rate investments (Moto, affordability)
Consensus EPS sources mix GAAP and non-GAAP, and GAAP EPS swings with equity-stake revaluations (Q2 +$1.6B)
reasoning: Primary docs show a fundamentally strong business. Q2'26 bookings were $58.0B (+22% cc, fourth straight 20%+ quarter, above the guide top), SBC-burdened non-GAAP EPS was $0.81 (+35%), TTM FCF $10.1B, and diluted shares fell ~4% YoY (src 1,4). The Q3 guide implies continued 18-22% growth and 28-35% EPS growth. Yet the stock is -29.5% in a year at ~15x trailing / ~14x P/FCF, because the market is discounting robotaxi disintermediation (Tesla Cybercab Austin debut, Waymo scaling, src 11) and the $10B AV spend plus a $14.8B Delivery Hero takeover funded by a EUR14.2B bridge (src 3,7). Insider signal: the CEO bought $10M in the open market at $70.96 on 2026-09-10 (Form 4, src 9), his first buy since 2022, and the COO bought $5.3M (src 11). My fair value is ~$84, from 18x a ~$4.70 NTM EPS at horizon and a 7% SBC-adjusted FCF yield. Both are deliberately below the peer median (26x fwd P/E across 11 marketplace/delivery/mobility peers) because the AV risk is structural through 2027. Scenarios: bear $50 (25%) / base $80 (50%) / bull $104 (25%). The mean is ~$78. I modelled each as a lognormal (sd ~0.22-0.25) and mixed them, which gives a ~35-38% effective vol, consistent with realized 35% plus AV event risk. That makes P(>=spot $70) ~0.61 and the median ~$77. The upward tilt reflects ~25% EPS compounding plus buybacks, which lift value even at a flat multiple. A fat left tail stays for the AV narrative. Research was limited: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage were unavailable (plan/rate limits), so peer multiples come from one aggregator, and its EV/EBITDA figures are trailing.
